The mandolute is a mandolin variant made in Philadelphia by Weymann & Son in the early twentieth century, a chordophone. Its construction is in fact that of an eight-string mandolin, tuned like a standard mandolin, with a scale length of about 13 inches (330 mm) to 13 7/8 inches (350 mm). The source does not describe how it is played, but the advertisements place this kind of mandolin in a formal parlour, showing young men and women making music together and dancing around a record player, which shows that it was used for social music-making at home.
